answers.falsifier: Done when a shaped fixture ticket kicked into FIXME, answered through answer_fixme, passes the FIXME gate with its plan bytes unchanged; an entry answer older than the latest kick-back is named; a decisions-plan ticket's FIXME n decision still counts; and the door refuses with nothing written an absent entry, blank text and no fixme list. Wrong intent if shaped tickets were meant to carry decisions after all (the shape check would be the defect).
answers.from_idea: none, because it was measured on ticket 78a600419a21, kicked into FIXME at PROVED (hollow_evidence_absent) with a shaped plan the cast door's _shape_lacks will not let carry a FIXME 1 decision
answers.how: In cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py: answer_fixme(ticket, n, text, by) writes fixme[n-1].answer={text,by,at} into the ticket's state file through ticket_file.write_state (the artifact door), refusing an absent entry, a blank text or no fixme list; crossing_fixme counts an entry's answer dated at or after the latest kick-back, beside the legacy FIXME n decisions; _main gains --answer-fixme <id> <n> <text>. Red-first proof cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/test_a_shaped_ticket_answers_its_fixme.py.
answers.traces_to: Law 8 (prove, then trust): a shaped ticket refused at PROVED must be able to answer and re-cross, or the only moves are plaster (writing past the shape check) or paralysis; Law 9: the red is fixed, not walked around.
answers.what: A shaped (outcomes) ticket kicked into FIXME answers each entry on the entry itself, through a build_inspector door, and the FIXME gate counts that answer, so the ticket can cross out of FIXME without a decisions line its plan shape forbids.
